checked_markdown_lines: Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): A truss is based on triangular geometry and its members are intended to work in axial tension or compression. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 1860-1873, 1885-1905, 1921-1997, 2007-2010, 2025-2031, and 7300-7415

Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): Loadbearing walls transmit compressive forces to the ground and are most vulnerable to forces perpendicular to their plane. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 1860-1873, 1885-1905, 1921-1997, 2007-2010, 2025-2031, and 7300-7415

Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): Openings in loadbearing walls weaken continuity and need a lintel or arch to carry load around the opening. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 1860-1873, 1885-1905, 1921-1997, 2007-2010, 2025-2031, and 7300-7415

Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): Building vertical support may be provided by loadbearing walls or by a column-and-beam framework. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 1860-1873, 1885-1905, 1921-1997, 2007-2010, 2025-2031, and 7300-7415

Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): Rigid floor diaphragms can transfer lateral loads to shear walls, braced frames, or rigid frames. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 1860-1873, 1885-1905, 1921-1997, 2007-2010, 2025-2031, and 7300-7415

Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): Shear walls, braced frames, and rigid frames can be used singly or in combination for lateral stability. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 1860-1873, 1885-1905, 1921-1997, 2007-2010, 2025-2031, and 7300-7415

Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): Rigid frames are useful where braced frames or shear walls would create unwanted barriers, but they are less efficient for lateral stability. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 1860-1873, 1885-1905, 1921-1997, 2007-2010, 2025-2031, and 7300-7415

Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): Taller buildings often need rigid frames supplemented by bracing mechanisms such as diagonal bracing or a rigid core. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 1860-1873, 1885-1905, 1921-1997, 2007-2010, 2025-2031, and 7300-7415

Building Construction Illustrated (5th Edition): Wood truss loads should be applied at panel points to avoid secondary bending, and bracing or diaphragm action may be needed for lateral wind or seismic forces. Locator: Building Construction Illustrated refined markdown lines 1860-1873, 1885-1905, 1921-1997, 2007-2010, 2025-2031, and 7300-7415

Hibbeler Statics 13th Edition: A truss is composed of slender members joined at their endpoints. Locator: Hibbeler Statics refined markdown lines 21217-21290, 21320-21378, 21693-21758, 21825-21921, and 21927-22271

Hibbeler Statics 13th Edition: Planar trusses are commonly used for roofs and bridges. Locator: Hibbeler Statics refined markdown lines 21217-21290, 21320-21378, 21693-21758, 21825-21921, and 21927-22271

Hibbeler Statics 13th Edition: Truss analysis assumes loads act at joints and joints are treated as pins. Locator: Hibbeler Statics refined markdown lines 21217-21290, 21320-21378, 21693-21758, 21825-21921, and 21927-22271

Hibbeler Statics 13th Edition: Under those assumptions, each member acts as a two-force member carrying tension or compression along its axis. Locator: Hibbeler Statics refined markdown lines 21217-21290, 21320-21378, 21693-21758, 21825-21921, and 21927-22271

Hibbeler Statics 13th Edition: A simple truss begins with a triangular unit and can be expanded by adding members and joints. Locator: Hibbeler Statics refined markdown lines 21217-21290, 21320-21378, 21693-21758, 21825-21921, and 21927-22271

Hibbeler Statics 13th Edition: Zero-force members may be identified by joint equilibrium when no external load or support reaction acts at the joint. Locator: Hibbeler Statics refined markdown lines 21217-21290, 21320-21378, 21693-21758, 21825-21921, and 21927-22271

Hibbeler Statics 13th Edition: Two non-collinear members at an unloaded joint are zero-force members. Locator: Hibbeler Statics refined markdown lines 21217-21290, 21320-21378, 21693-21758, 21825-21921, and 21927-22271

Hibbeler Statics 13th Edition: For three members at an unloaded joint, if two are collinear, the third is a zero-force member. Locator: Hibbeler Statics refined markdown lines 21217-21290, 21320-21378, 21693-21758, 21825-21921, and 21927-22271
